clue.text: Saint in detailed church paintings mostly

indicators.note: read as de-tailed: the church word loses its final letter

parts.note: a temple is a place of worship, a church

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the paintings word is used

parts.note: paintings are art

explanation.surface: A saint appears in the elaborate paintings that fill most of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed, cutting the last letter off TEMPLE to give TEMPL; 'mostly' trims ART to AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Templar is the hero of Leslie Charteris's stories, known by his nickname The Saint.

clue.text: Giant's caught out a queen

indicators.note: out says the letter for caught is dropped from the giant word

parts.note: titanic means giant, enormous
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A giant has been caught out by a queen, as in a chess game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes C (caught) from TITANIC, leaving TITANI; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Awfully trite? No, a matinee queen!

indicators.note: awfully suggests the following words are badly done, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic rejects a stale afternoon show, though its star is a matinee idol.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TRITE NO A MATINEE rearrange into the name of the French queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Antoinette was the queen consort of Louis XVI of France, executed in 1793.

clue.text: Most rowdy, outspoken king that is missing daughter

indicators.note: outspoken signals that the king's name is said out loud and written by its sound

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

indicators.note: missing tells us the daughter letter is taken away from the Latin phrase

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is

explanation.surface: The loudest, most vocal king is the one whose daughter has gone missing, a nod to Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outspoken' makes LEAR sound as LEER; 'missing' drops D from ID EST, leaving IEST. Lear fittingly lost daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: Leery is a spelling of lairy, British slang for loud, flashy and aggressive, so the superlative means rowdiest.

clue.text: Part of the clarinet family Jane Eyre is not happy with

definitions.meaning: the vibrating strip in a clarinet's mouthpiece

definitions.text: family Jane Eyre is not happy with
definitions.meaning: Mrs ... and her children mistreat the orphan Jane in Charlotte Brontë's novel

explanation.surface: Jane Eyre dislikes the woodwind section, a family of clarinets.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet sounds through a single cane strip, and Jane's cruel aunt and cousins bear that surname in the novel.

clue.text: Second wise man embraces another

indicators.note: embraces means the wise man's name is placed round the word for a second

parts.note: Solon was the wise Athenian lawgiver
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: In a moment one wise man hugs another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' looks like a stray word but is the definition: a second wise man, alongside the Athenian lawgiver. Mo, a moment, is a common crossword second.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon of Israel is the proverbial wise man, so he is a second one alongside Solon.

clue.text: More timid husky we hear Animal Farm might use

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: shyer means more timid and hoarse means husky in voice

explanation.surface: A rather timid sled dog seems to be the sort of thing a farm would use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husky' looks like the sled dog but means a rough voice, hoarse. Orwell's Animal Farm has the heavy horse Boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavy draught breed is a farm working animal, as is Boxer in Orwell's Animal Farm.

clue.text: The King's top couple upset about a literary critic

indicators.note: about says the turned name goes round the single letter
in a down clue the top couple are the first two letters of the King's name, and upset swaps their order

parts.note: The King is Elvis Presley's nickname

explanation.surface: The King's leading pair are disturbed by a literary critic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top couple upset' swaps the first two letters of ELVIS to give LEVIS; 'about' places that round A. The King is Elvis Presley's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: F. R. Leavis was an influential Cambridge critic of English literature.

clue.text: Noted piece has extra work on Satan, without taking sides

parts.note: one who moonlights has a second job on the side
taken as written

indicators.note: without taking sides means the outside letters of the word are left off

explanation.surface: A neutral composer moonlights on a piece about Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without taking sides' strips the first and last letters of SATAN to leave ATA. 'Noted' means set to musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 14 is known by this nickname, a famous musical composition.

clue.text: A Russian Countess's in-law regularly carries a toothbrush?

indicators.note: carries means the regular letters and the single letter hold the moustache between them
regularly means taking every other letter of the in-law word

parts.note: a toothbrush is a small clipped moustache, slang tash

explanation.surface: A Russian countess's relative by marriage often carries a toothbrush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes NA from iN-lAw; with A it 'carries' TASH, a moustache. 'toothbrush?' misleads: it means a toothbrush moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: Natasha Rostova of War and Peace is the daughter of Count Rostov, so a Russian countess.

clue.text: Coxless pair needs a cox to make this work

definitions.text: Coxless pair needs a cox to make this work

parts.words: Coxless pair needs a cox to make this work
parts.note: a two-oar rowing crew plus a coxswain makes a trio afloat, and the work is a comic novel

explanation.surface: Rowing advice: a coxless pair needs a cox to function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' seems to mean function but means a literary work, Jerome K. Jerome's 1889 comic novel of a Thames boating trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Two rowers plus a cox are a trio in a boat, which is the title of Jerome's comic novel.

clue.text: Sartre play you can't get out of?

definitions.meaning: Huis Clos, Sartre's 1944 drama, in its English title
a place without a way out

explanation.surface: A Sartre play is something you cannot escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartre's Huis Clos is known in English by this title, which also describes a room offering no way out.

clue.text: Play quietly with two boys

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
Eric is a boy's name
Les is another boy's name

explanation.surface: Two lads play quietly together.
explanation.definitionFit: Pericles, Prince of Tyre is a Shakespeare drama.

clue.text: Cite Homer breaking bounds by releasing energy

indicators.note: breaking bounds suggests letters running wild, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: x stands for by, as in measurements like 3 by 4

explanation.surface: Quoting Homer, someone breaks out of bounds by releasing energy.
explanation.walkthrough: X (by, as in 3 x 4) joins CITE HOMER, and 'breaking bounds' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, a reaction that gives off heat to its surroundings is described this way.

clue.text: Old lover in moving sonnet by an American poet

indicators.note: in says the old lover is placed inside the rearranged letters
moving means the letters of the words are shifted around

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An old flame features in a touching sonnet by an American poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like praise for a touching poem but is the anagram signal; 'by' is only a link joining the fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Sexton was a Pulitzer-winning American confessional poet.

clue.text: Not the first epic about Russia's capital city with a mausoleum

indicators.note: about says the trimmed epic goes round the capital letter
not the first means the opening letter of the epic word is dropped

parts.note: a saga is an epic tale

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something other than the first great epic about Russia's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the first' cuts SAGA to AGA; 'Russia's capital' is R; 'about' puts AGA round it. 'capital city' tempts as Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city is home to the Taj Mahal, a tomb built by Shah Jahan.

clue.text: Pilot supporting novelist, not quite six-footers

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits underneath, after the other piece
not quite means the novelist's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist
to fly is to pilot an aircraft

explanation.surface: A pilot backs a novelist who is not quite six feet tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footers' looks like tall people but means insects, which have six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are insects, and insects walk on six legs.

clue.text: Seafaring work that is low on love

indicators.note: on places the lowing word after the love letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
to low is to moo like a cow

explanation.surface: A sea story about cattle mooing at their beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: Herman Melville's 1847 novel of South Sea adventures is a book about seafaring.

clue.text: Work accommodating change with time off for a king

indicators.note: accommodating means the work word holds the other inside it

parts.note: an opus is a work

indicators.note: off means the time letter is taken away from the change word

parts.note: to edit is to change text

explanation.surface: A king's work accommodates change while taking time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with time off' removes T from EDIT, leaving EDI, which OPUS is 'accommodating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus was the mythical king of Thebes in Sophocles' tragedies.

clue.text: Attending to a sentence with difficulty

parts.note: to be at an event is to attend it
a stretch is slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: Attending to a sentence is hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' looks grammatical but means a jail term, a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means with effort, only by straining, as in managing something just about.

clue.text: Seasonal gift a lost child picked up

indicators.note: picked up suggests something caught by the ear, a word heard

parts.note: Hansel is one of the children lost in the forest in the fairy tale

explanation.surface: A gift at Christmas time, picked up by a lost child.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional New Year present, especially in Scotland, for luck at the start of the year.

clue.text: Fighter fights for honour, naked in Cervantes?

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet

indicators.note: naked means the word is stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: duels are fights to settle a point of honour

explanation.surface: A fighter battles for honour, naked, as if in Don Quixote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips DUELS to UEL. The definition is the first name 'in' the author Cervantes, who also fought at Lepanto.
explanation.definitionFit: Miguel de Cervantes is the full name of the author of Don Quixote, so this name appears in his.

clue.text: Weird and ominous day to trap a group of sibling killers

indicators.note: to trap means the other letters close around the single letter
weird says the following word is shaped strangely, rearranged

parts.note: the Ides of March was the fateful day of Caesar's murder

explanation.surface: A strange and ill-omened day sets out to catch a band of murderous siblings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weird' rearranges the letters of 'and'; 'to trap' holds the A inside. The Ides of March, when Caesar was killed, was famously ill-omened.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, the fifty daughters of Danaus, all sisters, murdered their husbands on their wedding night.

clue.text: Finish off leading female's horse

indicators.note: finish off means the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: the heroine is the leading female character

explanation.surface: Finish off the leading lady's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is slang for the drug, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is drug slang for the opiate, just as smack and H are.

clue.text: He fled Psyche skyward, annoyed

indicators.note: skyward means going up, so in a down clue the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sore can mean annoyed, aggrieved

explanation.surface: Annoyed, he fled from Psyche into the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: In the myth Cupid, the god of love, flew away after Psyche looked on him by lamplight.

clue.text: Novel line in request to reduce smoking?

indicators.note: in says the line letter is placed within the request

parts.note: put out more fags asks for cigarettes to be extinguished, fags being British slang for cigarettes

explanation.surface: A new line in a request to cut down on smoking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new but is the definition: Evelyn Waugh's 1942 novel. A fag is a cigarette in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn Waugh's 1942 wartime comic book is a work of fiction.

clue.text: Novel name gone round in varnish

parts.note: She is H. Rider Haggard's novel

indicators.note: gone round means the name word turns about and is read backwards

parts.note: to call is to name

explanation.surface: A novel's name has done the rounds, in varnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective but names Haggard's book; 'gone round' turns the name word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A resin secreted by the lac insect, dissolved to make a glossy coating for wood.

clue.text: Picture of Bond's curtailed island trip

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, with the last letter removed

parts.note: Skye is a Scottish island
to trip is to fall

explanation.surface: Bond takes a picture of a shortened trip to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' trims SKYE, the Hebridean island, to SKY.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2012 movie starring Daniel Craig is one of the James Bond films.
